analysis:
This PR changes only a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Startup/StartupPreloadTests.swift. The visible changes are a ReclaimableMemory helper (lines 96-118), a test that a short memory sample reclaims and re-samples before skipping (lines ~198-219), and a test that a short sample releases retained KV segments before the preload skips (lines 613-629). No production code is modified in the supplied evidence, so the change adds no new attack surface, auth, crypto, attestation, or data-exposure paths.

The tests exercise startup preload behavior. They cover no-eviction memory admission, reclaim-before-skip, fail-open versus fail-closed self-test retirement, and drain-time teardown of warm slots. The fail-closed retirement test (lines 1082-1162) checks that a retired model is removed from the advertised set and triggers a re-register. The tests use temp files and mock closures. They write fake HF snapshots under the real HF cache directory and clean them up with defer. This is a test-hygiene matter, not a security concern.

The retained T-041 prefix-cache threat is not weakened by these tests. The reclaim-before-skip test at line 613 references RetainingEngineStub and an engine.parkedBytes release, which implies a production reclaim hook. That hook is not visible here. The production reclaim of retained KV segments (the StartupPreloader reclaimBeforeSkip dependency and its ProviderLoop wiring) is not in the supplied evidence.

Open question for later integration: whether releasing retained prefix-cache or KV segments on a short memory sample changes the at-rest or staging reservation release paths named in the T-041 detection hint. Those are SSDPrefixCache.endAdoption/completeStaging and the EngineV2Bridge backstops. Production source for that behavior is not in this batch, so no conclusion can be drawn about it.
